headline: Immanuel Quickley recorded a triple-double on Friday with 24 points (8-of-15 FGs), 10 rebounds, 14 assists, one steal and four three-pointers in a 124-100 win over the Nets.
body: For the third time in his career and the first time since his second season, Quickley recorded a triple-double. He also set a season high for assists in what was his best performance of the season. Quickley has had a solid season, but this type of production isn’t something managers should expect to come often. Quickly has seen his usage increase with all the injuries they’re facing, which is a trend that should continue with Kawhi Leonard (knee) and RJ Barrett (hamstring) still sidelined.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Scottie Barnes led the Raptors with 34 points (11-of-20 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), one rebound, five assists, three blocks and two three-pointers against the Nets on Friday.
body: Barnes got off to a hot start in this game, scoring 22 points in the first half alone. He didn’t stay quite as hot after the break, but he was still able to turn in another strong scoring night. He has scored at least 30 points in three of his last five games while averaging 28.8 points, 4.8 rebounds, 4.8 assists, 2.2 blocks and 1.8 triples per game during this stretch. He’ll look to keep it going against the Nuggets on Sunday to close out the week.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Gui Santos (knee soreness) will not return against the Blazers on Friday.
body: Santos has already missed some time this year due to injuries. If he were to miss more time, look for Georges Niang to get more minutes, but it’s likely that the production gets spread around to other players and that there isn’t an obvious beneficiary to this injury.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Yanic Konan Niederhäuser (toe) will not return to Friday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: A right foot injury ended Niederhäuser’s 2025-26 season early and delayed his start to this year, and now it’s a right toe injury that will end his night early. This was only his fifth appearance this season, so hopefully this isn’t a long-term absence for him. Isaiah Jackson will fill out extra minutes off the bench.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jonathan Kuminga in 40 minutes, got 19 points (8-of-4 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, an assist, a steal, and a three in loss to Grizzlies on Friday.
body: Kuminga ramped up more of the usage with the absences of LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards and it resulted in a solid stat line in this one. He’s not someone who gets a lot of peripheral stats outside of the rebounds which limits his fantasy upside. While the two stars in Minnesota are still out, Kuminga should be rostered in redraft leagues.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Jaden McDaniels had 13 points (5-of-12 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, two assists, two steals, two blocks, a three, and four turnovers before fouling out on Friday.
body: The sell high window has likely closed somewhat after a fine scoring game. Even though he didn’t have the offensive explosion like he’s had the past couple games, he still filled up the box score and was very impactful in this game. This line could’ve been better had he not fouled out in the fourth quarter, but that is part of the deal with McDaniels.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Ayo Dosunmu got himself 27 points (10-of-17 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, three steals, a block, and four 3-pointers in the 114-109 loss to the Grizzlies.
body: With no LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards, Ayo Dosunmu took more of a charge offensively which helped his performance on the court. He hit his shots in this one which obviously helps, but he was the reason why the Wolves weren’t getting blown out and back in this game in the third quarter. While LaMelo and Anthony Edwards are out, he should be rostered in redraft leagues.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Collin Murray-Boyles provided a boost off the bench with 19 points (4-of-9 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist, two steals and one three-pointer against the Nets on Friday.
body: For a second straight game, CMB came off the bench, with rookie Allen Graves getting the starting nod. CMB may eventually return to the starting unit, but he has been effective as a reserve, with this being a strong outing for him as he matched his season high for scoring. Regardless of when his minutes come, CMB will continue to be a strong fantasy option when he’s on the floor for Toronto.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Cam Spencer put up 16 points (7-of-14 FGs), six rebounds, four assists, three steals, two blocks, and two 3-pointers in the win over the Timberwolves on Wednesday.
body: Cam Spencer excels in his role as a bench scorer and being one of the best shooters in the NBA. Despite the lackluster athleticism, his ability to decelerate and take smart shots is why he’s still in the NBA. He attacks the glass, he can pass, he can defend, and he’s a psychopath competitor. He’s a streamer in redraft leagues, and in deeper dynasty leagues, he should be a good player despite him being older for being a newer player in the NBA.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Cedric Coward got himself 22 points (9-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals, two blocks, and two 3-pointers in the 114-109 win over the Timberwolves.
body: Cedric Coward has had an awesome season, and he was good in this one. He didn’t get as many rebounds as you were wanting, but it’s hard to complain given his production this season. He’s one of the rising stars at the wing position in the NBA and should continue to get better.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Ja’Kobe Walter (quad) will not return to Friday’s game against the Nets.
body: Walter has been a starter for most of the season but won’t be available for the rest of this game. Jamison Battle, Jamal Shead and Alijah Martin are all options to take on extra minutes to close out this game.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jazz will start Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Josh Green, Ace Bailey, and Jusuf Nurkić on Friday against the Nuggets.
body: Nurkić returned from his toe injury and will go into the starting lineup in his first game back. Mo Bamba has been ruled out with an illness, but as long as Nurkić is healthy, he should be in the starting lineup for the Jazz this season. Mo Bamba

headline: Spurs will start De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell, Julian Champagnie, and Victor Wembanyama on Friday.
body: De’Aaron Fox will return to the starting lineup and Dylan Harper will come off the bench in Friday’s game against the Lakers. We’ll see if this is permanent, but this is the lineup they played last season. Harper returned from his injury earlier than expected, so that could be a reason why there’s no change in the lineup.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Blazers will start Jrue Holiday, Sidy Cissoko, Deni Avdija, Toumani Camara, and Donovan Clingan on Friday vs the Warriors.
body: Damian Lillard will sit out Friday’s game, so Jrue Holiday will start in his place. If Holiday is on your waiver wire, and you have space in your active lineup, he’s worth grabbing in redraft leagues.
author: Brian Taylor Damian Lillard

headline: De’Aaron Fox (shin) is available to play against the Lakers on Friday.
body: Fox will be back following a two-game absence. Harrison Barnes started in his place but should return to the bench. Dylan Harper (hip) will also be back, giving the Spurs their healthiest lineup in a while.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Dylan Harper (hip) will be available to play against the Lakers on Friday.
body: The expectation is that he would be out for a couple weeks, instead he’s back early from his injury. The result of this is that Stephon Castle should take a bit of a step back, as well as Julian Champagnie, Harrison Barnes, Jordan McLaughlin, and Ja’Kobi Gillespie. Harper has had a great season averaging 18.4 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 4.5 assists.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Mavs will start Cooper Flagg, Caleb Martin, Zaccharie Risacher, P.J. Washington, and Daniel Gafford against the Suns on Friday.
body: Washington will re-enter the starting lineup with the absence of Kyrie Irving. Cooper Flagg will start at PG but we’ll likely see some more minutes for Walter Clayton and Marcus Sasser. P.J. is a streamer for redraft leagues and not a must roster.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Jaxson Hayes (knee) is available to play against the Nuggets on Friday.
body: Hayes will be back following a one-game absence. That also coincides with the season debut of Jusuf Nurkić, though it’s unclear what his role will be in his first game. Hayes could start, though he will at least play a significant role off the bench.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jusuf Nurkić (toe) will make his season debut against the Nuggets on Friday.
body: The Jazz have sorely missed Nurkić’s passing and presence in the paint on the offensive end. If Nurkić is available in your redraft leagues, he’s worth looking at given how he’s used on the offensive end. His passing will help unlock a lot of the Will Hardy offense that involves a lot of off ball movement.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Mo Bamba (illness) has been ruled out against the Nuggets on Friday.
body: Bamba will be sidelined for this game, but with both Jaxson Hayes and Jusuf Nurkić healthy and available, Bamba may not have played much, if he saw the floor at all. The return of Nurkić should eliminate any streaming value Bamba held when he ends up returning to the lineup.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin) is available to play against the Knicks on Friday.
body: Giannis was initially listed as probable for this game as he continues to manage a groin issue. That has limited his production, as he had 32 points and 14 rebounds in their last game on Wednesday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Dennis Schröder (hamstring) is out for Saturday’s matchup with the Nets.
body: Schröder is past his two-week re-evaluation period, so it’s unclear when he’ll be able to return. Christian Anderson should continue to handle additional minutes until Schröder is back.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Steven Adams (knee) is questionable to play against the 76ers on Saturday.
body: Adams has filled out the backup center minutes for Houston over their last few games after missing a few weeks with a calf injury. If he isn’t available, Clint Capela will take on extra minutes in place of Adams.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Grayson Allen (concussion) is questionable to play against the Nets on Saturday.
body: Allen has missed four straight games and could remain out for a fifth against Brooklyn. Sion James, who isn’t worth rostering in fantasy basketball, should continue to start if Allen misses another game.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Kevin Porter Jr. (reconditioning) has been ruled out against the Wizards on Saturday.
body: KPJ signed with Orlando earlier this week, but they won’t rush him out until he’s ready. Eventually, he’ll provide depth in the backcourt, with his next chance to debut coming on Sunday against the Pistons.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Anthony Black (back) is questionable for Saturday’s matchup with the Wizards.
body: If Black is sidelined against Washington, more playing time could be available for Jalen Suggs and Tristan da Silva.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Yang Hansen (ankle) is questionable for Friday’s matchup with the Warriors.
body: Hansen hasn’t played much of a role in Portland’s rotation, so his availability isn’t impactful to fantasy hoops managers.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: ESPN’s Dave McMenamin reports that Austin Reaves (heel) is available for Friday’s matchup with the Spurs.
body: Reaves will return following a five-game absence, and that should mean a reduced role for Quentin Grimes. Fantasy managers who have been streaming Grimes should hold him in case Reaves suffers any setbacks.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Kyrie Irving (knee) is questionable for Friday’s matchup with the Suns.
body: Irving is on the injury report for left knee injury management, and he’s in danger of sitting out against Phoenix. If Irving is sidelined, Cooper Flagg would presumably handle increased playmaking responsibilities, with Walter Clayton Jr. and Max Christie absorbing Irving’s vacated minutes in the backcourt.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: LaMelo Ball (ankle) is out for Friday’s matchup with the Grizzlies.
body: Ball suffered the ankle injury on Wednesday, and it will cost him at least one game. His absence could mean a spot start for Bones Hyland with more minutes available for Terrence Shannon Jr.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Damian Lillard (calf) is out for Friday’s matchup with the Warriors.
body: Lillard is dealing with right calf tightness/soreness that will keep him out for at least one contest. His absence could mean a spot start for Jrue Holiday and potentially more run for Scoot Henderson. Lillard’s next chance to return will come on Sunday against the Pelicans.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Jalen Smith (gastrointestinal illness) has been upgraded to probable for Saturday’s matchup with the Pacers.
body: Smith sat out Wednesday against the Hornets, but he’s on track to face the Bulls’ Central Division rival on Saturday. He and Nic Claxton should share responsibilities at center.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Miles McBride (adductor) and Jordan Clarkson (foot) are out for Friday’s matchup with the Heat.
body: McBride has missed two straight games, and Clarkson has missed four in a row. Across the last two games, Jose Alvarado has seen his production and playing time increase, averaging 16 points across 20.5 minutes.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: OG Anunoby (calf) is out for Friday’s matchup with the Heat.
body: Anunoby received a doubtful tag on Thursday due to a left calf strain, so his absence isn’t surprising. He’ll sit a fourth straight game, which should mean another start for Landry Shamet. Shamet should remain on the streaming radar until Anunoby is healthy.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Larry Nance Jr. (ankle) is probable for Friday’s matchup with the 76ers.
body: Nance Jr. is expected to take the court after getting injured in Monday’s win over the Thunder, but his availability doesn’t impact fantasy hoops due to Nance Jr.'s limited role in the rotation.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Dean Wade (hamstring) is questionable for Friday’s matchup with the Pacers.
body: Wade is on the injury report for left hamstring injury management, and he could get a maintenance day for the first leg of Philly’s back-to-back set. If Wade is ruled out, more minutes could be available for Jabari Walker and Dominick Barlow.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Kasparas Jakučionis (ankle) has been ruled out of Friday’s matchup with the Pistons.
body: Jakučionis is dealing with left ankle tenosynovitis which will sideline him for at least one game. Ryan Rollins could absorb the vacated minutes.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Jaxson Hayes (knee) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Nuggets.
body: Hayes did not play in Monday’s loss to the Lakers, leaving the Jazz to rely on a rotation of Mo Bamba and Kyle Filipowski at center. With Jusuf Nurkić (toe) also questionable, Bamba may get fewer minutes, while Filipowski could fall out of the rotation entirely.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jusuf Nurkić (toe) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Nuggets.
body: Injured during the preseason, Nurkić could potentially make his first appearance of the season on Friday. With Jaxson Hayes (knee) also questionable, Utah’s center rotation could be the healthiest it’s been all season. Mo Bamba has been the starter, with Kyle Filipowski serving as his backup in Monday’s loss to the Lakers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tobi Lawal (groin) and Tarik Biberović (heel) are out for Friday’s game against the Suns.
body: Lawal and Biberović remain out, with the latter yet to make his NBA debut. Their absences do not affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Sergio de Larrea (knee) is out for Friday’s game against the Suns.
body: De Larrea suffered a sprained knee during the first week of the regular season and hasn’t played since. His absence has factored into Walter Clayton Jr. playing rotation minutes off the bench, and that’s unlikely to change anytime soon.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Dylan Harper (hip) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Lakers.
body: When Harper initially injured his hip, the expectation was that he would miss between two and three weeks. The second-year guard could be back in just over a week, as he’s questionable for Friday night. Harper’s minutes could be restricted if he’s allowed to play, possibly meaning that Julian Champagnie remains in the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Aaron Fox (shin) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Lakers.
body: Fox has missed the Spurs’ last two games with a shin contusion, resulting in Harrison Barnes moving into the starting lineup. Fox’s absence has also left Stephon Castle as the lone point guard in the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Austin Reaves (heel) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Reaves has missed the Lakers’ last five games with a heel injury, and there’s hope that he’ll be able to play on Friday. Quentin Grimes has been the replacement in the starting lineup and should hold onto that role until Reaves returns.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: LaMelo Ball (ankle) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: Ball sprained his left ankle in the fourth quarter of Wednesday’s win over the Thunder and needed help to return to the bench. The good news is that he’s questionable for Friday’s game, suggesting the injury wasn’t too severe. If Ball can’t play, Bones Hyland could replace him in the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Stewart (hip) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Stewart, who played 14 minutes off the bench in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers, is dealing with a sore right hip. If he can’t play on Friday, Quinten Post would likely get more minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Joel Embiid (illness) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Pacers.
body: Embiid has missed Philadelphia’s last two games, with Jabari Walker replacing him in the starting lineup. Walker will head to the bench if Embiid is available on Friday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaylen Brown (hamstring) is out for Friday’s game against the Pacers.
body: Brown exited Wednesday’s win over the Heat in the second quarter with a left hamstring injury. The 76ers have not provided a concrete update on the injury’s severity, listing Brown as out for Friday’s game due to left hamstring injury management. Dean Wade started the second half, but Kentavious Caldwell-Pope replaced Brown in the starting lineup when Brown missed two games earlier this month.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Miles McBride (adductor) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Heat.
body: McBride has missed New York’s last two games, leading to more playing time for Jose Alvarado. Expect the same if McBride remains out on Friday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Andre Drummond (head) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Heat.
body: Drummond suffered a head injury in the first half of Wednesday’s win over the Cavaliers and did not return. If he can’t play on Friday, the Knicks will turn to James Wiseman as the backup center.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jordan Clarkson (foot) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Heat.
body: Clarkson has missed New York’s last three games due to right plantar fasciitis. If he remains out, Pacôme Dadiet should once again play rotation minutes off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: OG Anunoby (calf) is doubtful for Friday’s game against the Heat.
body: Anunoby has missed New York’s last three games and appears likely to miss a fourth as he deals with a strained left calf. Landry Shamet has performed well as the replacement in the starting lineup, and he’s worth streaming until Anunoby returns.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Moritz Wagner (knee) is out for Friday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Wagner exited Wednesday’s game against the Bucks in the first half and did not return. His absence for the entirety of Friday’s game likely means more minutes for Noah Clowney and Grant Nelson, but neither should be rostered in most redraft leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Andrew Wiggins (ankle) is probable for Friday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Wiggins is dealing with a sprained right ankle, but the probable tag suggests that he’ll take on his usual bench role. If Wiggins can’t play, fellow reserve Simone Fontecchio may pick up additional minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin) is probable for Friday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Antetokounmpo has been dealing with right groin tendinitis for a few games, which led to him missing Sunday’s win over the Thunder. However, he returned to play 36 minutes in Wednesday’s loss to the 76ers. With the probable tag, fantasy managers should expect Giannis to take on his usual workload against the Knicks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Mitchell Robinson (illness) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Hawks.
body: Robinson has missed Boston’s last three games with an illness. However, while he was immediately ruled out of those games, the Celtics center is questionable on the initial report for Friday. If Robinson remains out, the Celtics will continue to rely on Neemias Queta, Luka Garza and Chris Cenac Jr.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Damian Lillard had a monster 29 points (7-of-20 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, two steals, and five 3-pointers in the win over the Spurs on Wednesday.
body: He had a couple down games, so it’s good to see him bounce back. Damian Lillard continues to show up in big moments and was good in this one. He gave you a real boost from the free throw line and a good bump in points. On the season, he hasn’t been as efficient from the field compared to previous seasons, but considering his age and injury history, it might be part of the deal with Lillard at this point in his career.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Sidy Cissoko got himself 16 points (6-of-14 FGs), four rebounds, two assists, two steals, a block, and four 3-pointers against the Spurs on Wednesday.
body: While the stats don’t exactly show it, he’s been good for Portland this season and has been great at balancing out the lineup with Ja Morant injured. He’s had good outings from a fantasy perspective in three of the past four games. He’s more of a streamer but in deeper leagues given that he doesn’t put up a lot of numbers when he’s on the court. In dynasty leagues, he’s a solid deeper league option who could provide sneaky value.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Deni Avdija put up 33 points (11-of-21 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), 12 rebounds, seven assists, two steals, and five 3-pointers in the 111-116 win over the Spurs on Wednesday.
body: Avdija’s rim pressure was on full display which was a big reason why the Blazers were as competitive as they were. Deni on the season has been exactly what you would’ve hoped for apart from the free throw percentage which is at 69.5% on the season. That should improve, but he has had seasons shooting in the 70’s from the free throw line.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Devin Vassell had 18 points (6-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, two steals, a block, and three 3-pointers in the loss to the Blazers on Wednesday.
body: Vassell did a good job being a tertiary scorer in this one which was badly needed. The Spurs only had three players that could consistently score with Wemby, Castle, and Vassell in this game. He even filled up the box score with the peripheral stats that you don’t often get from him. While Fox is out, Vassell should be receive a bump in scoring.

headline: Stephon Castle got himself 20 points (6-of-18 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, nine assists, and two 3-pointers on Wednesday.
body: Castle was a monster in this one and was instrumental in the Spurs staying close in this game. He filled up the stat sheet while hitting his free throws. That’s two good games in a row for Castle, and if Fox misses more time, we could see a potential short sell high window with Fox and Harper out. If not, enjoy the production while it lasts.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Victor Wembanyama had 44 points (17-of-30 FGs, 7-of-10 FTs), 16 rebounds, three assists, a steal, two blocks, and three 3-pointers in the 111-116 loss to the Blazers on Wednesday.
body: Wembanyama returned form his back injury and based on his stat line, you wouldn’t have been able to tell the difference. He was completely dominant again and continues to his MVP campaign. He’s a complete cheat code in fantasy and unless he gets hurt, he will continue to put up video games numbers every game and completely alter the geometry of the court.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Emanuel Sharp finished Wednesday’s loss to the Warriors with nine points (3-of-6 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers.
body: Zach LaVine was not available for Wednesday’s game due to a knee injury. Instead of Malik Monk (five points, four assists and one steal), Kings head coach Doug Christie prioritized defense and started Sharp. The rookie shot the ball well, making three of his six attempts. However, Sharp’s struggles to defend without fouling landed him in foul trouble, and he eventually fouled out in the fourth quarter. If LaVine remains out, Sharp could get more starts, as a low-usage guard who seems to fit well alongside Darius Acuff Jr.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keegan Murray recorded 18 points (8-of-19 FGs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: Murray appears to be making strides offensively after a slow start to the season, as he extended his streak of games with double-digit scoring to five. The 18 points were a season high for the Kings forward, who is shooting 49.2 percent from the field over the last five games. Murray’s free-throw percentage during this stretch (50.0) is low, but he’s attempted four foul shots total, making two. His season-long fantasy value remains low, but things may be looking up for managers who refused to throw in the towel.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Acuff Jr. accounted for 22 points (9-of-24 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, nine assists and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: Acuff’s efficiency took a hit on Wednesday, as he needed 24 shots to score 22 points and committed five turnovers. However, given some of the stout individual defenders on the Warriors’ roster, this performance isn’t surprising. Even with the turnover concerns, Acuff has provided top-75 value in nine-cat formats. With the Kings all-in on the rookie guard, he’ll have every opportunity to maintain that production level, if not improve it.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Domantas Sabonis tallied 27 points (8-of-9 FGs, 10-of-12 FTs), 10 rebounds, six assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: In addition to recording at least 12 rebounds in seven straight games, Sabonis extended his double-double streak to four games on Wednesday. After struggling to start the season, the Kings’ center has been more productive recently, benefiting fantasy managers. Over the last week, Sabonis has averaged 20.3 points, 13.8 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game while shooting 70.7 percent from the field and 80.8 percent from the foul line. Sbaonis doesn’t offer much defensive production, which limits his fantasy ceiling.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jarrett Allen amassed 10 points (5-of-7 FGs), five rebounds, one assist and two steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: James Harden accumulated 28 points (7-of-19 FGs, 13-of-14 FTs), one rebound, five assists, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Donovan Mitchell recorded 30 points (12-of-24 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, four steals, two blocks and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jose Alvarado amassed 21 points (8-of-10 FGs), one rebound, three assists, two steals and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Cavaliers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Brunson tallied 19 points (6-of-22 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, five assists and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Cavaliers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Josh Hart recorded 15 points (6-of-14 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, 12 assists, three steals, two blocks and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Cavaliers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Mikal Bridges tallied 19 points (9-of-15 FGs), eight rebounds, two assists, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Cavaliers.
body: While his production has been inconsistent recently, Bridges has been better overall than he was at the start of the season. Wednesday’s performance was his best yet, with the Knicks’ wing scoring 15 of his season-high 19 points in the second quarter. Add in the rebounds and field-goal percentage, and this was a good night for Bridges. He’ll look to string together two straight quality games when the Knicks host the Heat on Friday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: The Spurs will start Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell, Julian Champagnie, Harrison Barnes, and Victor Wembanyama on Wednesday against the Blazers.
body: Wemby returns to the starting lineup after his brief absence with his back injury, and Luke Kornet will return to the bench. Kornet is nothing more than a deeper league guy, and Wemby will return to tormenting teams on offense and defense.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: The Kings will start Darius Acuff, Emanuel Sharp, De’Andre Hunter, Keegan Murray, and Domantas Sabonis against the Warriors on Wednesday.
body: Zach LaVine was rule out of Wednesday’s game, so rookie Emmanuel Sharp will get the start. Sharp is just a streamer for 3’s, but shouldn’t be a priority in most leagues. A lot of his impact doesn’t show up in the counting stats, and even dating back to college, he wasn’t a stat stuffer.
author: Brian Taylor Zach LaVine

headline: Matas Buzelis tallied a team-high 24 points (8-of-15 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs) and five rebounds over 34 minutes to power the Bulls to a 107-105 win over the Hornets on Wednesday.
body: - George Bissell

headline: Brandon Miller amassed a game-high 35 points (13-of-25 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, one assist and three steals over 34 minutes in Wednesday’s loss to the Bulls.
body: - George Bissell

headline: Andre Drummond (head) is questionable to return to Wednesday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Drummond took a shot to the head during the second quarter of Wednesday’s game. While Drummond finished the half, James Wiseman replaced Karl-Anthony Towns when the Knicks’ starting center took his customary third-quarter break.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Josh Giddey posted a double-double with 12 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 11 rebounds and seven assists over 33 minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Hornets.
body: - George Bissell

headline: Moussa Diabaté recorded a double-double with 14 points (5-of-9 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 14 rebounds, two assists and one steal over 38 minutes in Wednesday’s loss to the Bulls.
body: - George Bissell

headline: Victor Wembanyama (back) will be available against the Trail Blazers on Wendesday.
body: Wembanyama will return from a one game absence and likely return to the starting lineup. He’s having an unbelievable season averaging 29.9 PPG, 12.3 REB, 3.2 AST, and 3.9 blocks on the season.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Moritz Wagner (knee) will not return to Wednesday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Wagner played just under four minutes in the first half of Wednesday’s game before being shut down due to a sore left knee. Grant Nelson may get additional minutes off the bench, but it is unlikely to affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin) is probable for Wednesday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Antetokounmpo was upgraded to probable and thus is likely to suit up against the 76ers Wednesday, which is great news for fantasy managers. The 31-year-old forward missed Sunday’s game against the Thunder with right groin tendonitis. Bobby Portis will head back to the bench with Antetokounmpo in the starting lineup.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Joel Embiid (illness) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Heat.
body: No surprise here as Embiid was ruled out after he was initially listed as doubtful with an illness. Jabari Walker should start again in his absence. Walker had 10 points, five rebounds, two assists and one steal in 20 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Kevin Porter Jr. is finalizing a two-year contract with the Orlando Magic.
body: Porter was waived by the Bucks in October. The 26-year-old guard also met with the Nuggets before deciding to sign with the Magic this week, according to Charania. Porter figures to provide Orlando with backcourt depth. He averaged 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds and 7.4 assists last season.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Miles McBride (adductor) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: McBride was ruled out with left adductor tightness. Jose Alvarado and Landry Shamet will see more minutes and usage with McBride sidelined.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Josh Hart (shoulder) is probable for Wednesday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Hart was upgraded to probable Wednesday afternoon. The 31-year-old guard is likely to play despite dealing with a sprained right shoulder. Hart could be counted on more on the offensive end Wednesday if Jalen Brunson (illness) is ruled out.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Karl-Anthony Towns (knee) is probable for Wednesday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Towns was upgraded to probable Wednesday afternoon. It’s good news for the 31-year-old center, who is dealing with right knee inflammation. Towns could see a boost in usage if Jalen Brunson (illness) is ruled out.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jalen Brunson (illness) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Brunson popped up on the injury report Wednesday afternoon as questionable with an illness. He’s potentially on the wrong side of questionable here. Jose Alvarado would start and be worth streaming if Brunson is ruled out.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Michael Scotto of Hoops Hype reports that Markelle Fultz is joining the Raptors’ G League affiliate.
body: Fultz spent time with the Raptors’ G League affiliate Raptors 905 last season and even made five appearances with their parent club. The former No. 1 pick in the 2017 NBA Draft, Fultz has spent time with four different teams in his nine-year career.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Grayson Allen (concussion) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Bulls.
body: Allen is set to miss his fourth game in a row with a concussion. Sion James will continue starting in his absence, but doesn’t provide enough fantasy value to be worth streaming in most leagues.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Christian Braun notched 15 points (5-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Mavericks.
body: Braun recorded a full stat line on Tuesday, and he continues to provide top-100 fantasy value. He’s reached double figures in scoring in seven straight games and has been a top-50 player over the last two weeks. After a subpar 2025-26 season in which he played a career-low 44 games, Braun has rebounded nicely. And given the lack of production from Denver’s bench, there are likely to be even more opportunities for Braun to make some things happen as a scorer.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cameron Johnson accounted for 17 points (5-of-15 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Mavericks.
body: Matching his season-high with four three-pointers, Johnson is 8-of-16 from beyond the arc over his last two games. His overall field-goal percentage against the Mavericks wasn’t good, but fantasy managers should be encouraged that Johnson kept shooting instead of passing up looks. Unfortunately, Johnson didn’t record any defensive stats, but he is averaging 1.2 steals per game.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jamal Murray accumulated 20 points (6-of-17 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Mavericks.
body: After torching the Bulls for 45 points on Sunday, Murray cooled off considerably on Tuesday. The Mavericks certainly deserve credit, as their defense throughout the night made life difficult for Murray individually and the Nuggets as a whole. He’s scored at least 20 points in seven of his last eight games, so one bad night isn’t enough to sound the alarm. Murray will look to bounce back on Friday against the Jazz.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nikola Jokić finished Tuesday’s loss to the Mavericks with 18 points (6-of-14 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), 11 rebounds, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer.
body: Jokić recorded his 13th double-double of the season, but this was far from a vintage performance for the three-time MVP. He committed five turnovers, the most in a game for The Joker since recording seven in a November 16 loss to the Suns. Jokić remains among the most valuable players in fantasy basketball regardless of format, but he’s come back to the pack somewhat after multiple seasons of dominance.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Caleb Martin tallied 13 points (5-of-8 FGs), four rebounds, four assists, five steals, two blocks and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Nuggets.
body: Rostered in 11 percent of Yahoo leagues, Martin finished Tuesday’s victory with a stat line that will make fantasy managers take notice. He recorded a career-high five steals, along with two blocked shots, while also shooting well from the field and beyond the arc. Martin has nine steals over his last two games and has recorded multiple steals in four of his last five appearances. The only negative is that Dallas plays only one more game this week, Friday in Phoenix.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: P.J. Washington (illness) recorded 14 points (6-of-11 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Nuggets.
body: Washington returned to the Mavericks’ rotation after a two-game absence, but not as a starter. However, the reserve role did not negatively affect his production, and Washington still played 25 minutes. Zaccharie Risacher (12/6/1/2/1 with one three-pointer) played 21 minutes as the starter, so the rotation could change as soon as Friday’s game against the Suns.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kyrie Irving amassed 11 points (5-of-19 FGs), five rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Nuggets.
body: Irving struggled with his shot, making one of eight three-point attempts. However, he was better offensively in the second half, dishing out five of his six assists to help the Mavericks pull away. Irving entered Tuesday shooting 45.9 percent from the field, so there shouldn’t be much concern after his 5-of-19 night against the Nuggets. Dallas ends its Week 6 with a game against the Suns on Friday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cooper Flagg finished Tuesday’s win over the Nuggets with 24 points (8-of-17 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), six rebounds, 12 assists and one three-pointer.
body: In addition to recording his sixth double-double of the season, Flagg matched his career high in steals, which he initially set in a November 8 win over the Nets. Just as impressive, the reigning Rookie of the Year committed just one turnover in 31 minutes. Flagg has provided first-round fantasy value, and he is well positioned to continue producing at a high level for the Mavericks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Trae Young accounted for 17 points (4-of-9 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), 12 assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
body: Young continues to take a step back as a scorer, which is by design. The Wizards want him to focus more on setting up others, and he did that very well on Tuesday. Young recorded 12 assists while committing one turnover in one of his most efficient efforts of the season. However, the issue isn’t Young shooting the ball less; it’s that his accuracy has taken a hit. Tuesday’s 4-of-9 effort will help, but he’s still shooting 36.8 percent from the field this season.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: AJ Dybantsa finished Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics with 20 points (7-of-18 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), 11 rebounds, seven assists and two three-pointers.
body: A 20-point scorer in four of his last five games, Dybantsa has recorded three double-doubles during this stretch. Add in the seven assists, and this was a good night for those rostering the rookie, even if he didn’t record any defensive stats. Dybantsa still isn’t providing top-100 per-game value, but he’s not far from that threshold.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Wendell Carter Jr. finished Tuesday’s loss to the Pistons with nine points (3-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 13 rebounds, two assists, three steals and one three-pointer.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Desmond Bane accounted for 21 points (8-of-13 FGs), one rebound, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Pistons.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Franz Wagner accumulated 20 points (9-of-20 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), nine rebounds, six assists and one block in Tuesday’s loss to the Pistons.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ausar Thompson produced six points (3-of-3 FGs), 10 rebounds, seven assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Magic.
body: While he doesn’t offer much as a scorer, Thompson’s ability to fill a stat line is what keeps his category league value in a good place. In addition to recording a season-high four blocks, the Pistons wing hit double digits in rebounds for the sixth time while also dishing out seven assists. Adding a dependable shot to his game would do wonders for Thompson’s fantasy value, but that doesn’t seem likely anytime soon.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kevin Huerter amassed 13 points (6-of-10 FGs), six rebounds, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Magic.
body: Since moving into the Pistons’ starting lineup following Duncan Robinson’s quad injury, Huerter has scored in double figures in three of five games. Limited to two points in Sunday’s loss to the Hawks, “Red Velvet” bounced back with a solid performance in Orlando. Huerter is rostered in 22 percent of Yahoo leagues, a fair number given his production, even with Robinson sidelined.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Joe finished Tuesday’s win over the Magic with 21 points (8-of-15 FGs), four rebounds, one steal and five three-pointers.
body: Joe made his first start of the season on Tuesday after Cade Cunningham (knee) was scratched late. One game removed from scoring 19 points, Joe recorded his first 20-point stat line of the season, shooting 5-of-11 from beyond the arc. The Pistons host the Bucks on Friday. And while that may be enough time for Cunningham to return, there may still be value in holding onto Joe, given how much the Bucks have struggled this season.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Daniss Jenkins recorded 15 points (6-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, 10 assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Magic.
body: With Cade Cunningham (knee) being a late scratch, Jenkins moved into the starting point guard role on Tuesday. While he did commit five turnovers, the third-year guard hit double digits in assists for the first time this season and the fifth time in his career. This wasn’t Jenkins’ most efficient outing, but he provided solid value in multiple categories. At a minimum, he should be rostered until Jalen Duren returns from his hamstring injury.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: P.J. Washington (illness) is available for Tuesday’s game against the Nuggets.
body: Washington is back after a two-game absence. His return means that Zaccharie Risacher will come off the bench after starting the last two games.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Victor Wembanyama (back) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Wembanyama did not play in Monday’s win over the Kings, and while he was expected to be available on Wednesday, the Spurs are officially listing him as questionable. If Wemby remains out, Luke Kornet would get another start after recording his first double-double of the season on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Aaron Fox (shin) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Fox did not play in Monday’s win over the Kings. While reports said on Monday that he’s expected to return Wednesday night, the Spurs are listing their point guard as questionable. If Fox remains out, Stephon Castle will run the point, with Harrison Barnes remaining in the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Derrick White, Paul George, Jayson Tatum, Sam Hauser and Neemias Queta will start Tuesday’s game against the Wizards.
body: George is back after missing Sunday’s loss to the Warriors. As a result, Hugo González heads to the bench, with Sam Hauser getting another start.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tre Mann (illness) is available for Tuesday’s game against the Celtics.
body: Mann is good to go after initially being listed as questionable. However, he has not been a consistent part of the Wizards’ rotation, so this news doesn’t affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Daniss Jenkins, Isaiah Joe, Kevin Huerter, Ausar Thompson and John Collins will start Tuesday’s game against the Magic.
body: The Pistons won’t have Cade Cunningham, who’s been ruled out with a knee injury. He’s been replaced in the starting lineup by Joe, which means that Jenkins will run the point. Both players are worth streaming where available.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cade Cunningham (knee) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Magic.
body: Cunningham is out after initially being listed as probable for Tuesday’s game. Daniss Jenkins, who is already in the starting lineup, should see his role expand. He’s worth streaming, especially on a three-game night.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaylin Williams (back spasms) out Wednesday vs. Timberwolves.
body: Williams will miss his second straight contest due to lower back spasms. The forward/center has already missed seven games this season with a lower back injury. Kenrich Williams will likely see increased minutes with the 6'9" center out.
author: Shawn Robinson

headline: Alex Caruso (hip) is not on the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Caruso is back after missing Oklahoma City’s last three games. His return gives the Thunder much-needed wing depth for a team hit hard by injuries.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Yaxel Lendeborg (illness) questionable for Wednesday vs. Kings.
body: The rookie showed up on the injury report a day before the matchup against Sacramento. Fantasy managers will need to keep an eye out for updates closer to Wednesday’s tip off.
author: Shawn Robinson

headline: Jake LaRavia recorded a double-double on Monday with 15 points (6-of-10 FGs), 10 rebounds, one assist, two steals and one three-pointer against the Jazz.
body: LaRavia returned to the starting lineup after two games as a reserve. He took advantage of the opportunity by setting a new season high for scoring and recording his first double-double of the season. LaRavia’s scoring is down from last season, but he has been a decent source of steals. However, that isn’t enough for him to be considered a must-roster player, even if this was a strong performance.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Quentin Grimes contributed nine points (1-of-8 FGs), three rebounds, eight assists, one block and one three-pointer against the Jazz on Monday.
body: Grimes struggled with his shot in what could be his final start before Austin Reaves (heel) returns to the lineup, but he made up for it with his passing. He surpassed his season high of seven assists, which he set in his previous outing. In the three games since he scored 47 points, Grimes has scored a total of 42 points. It was a fun stretch for him as a starter, and if he gets the chance again, he’ll be worth streaming. However, initial reports had Reaves returning for either this game against Utah or for Friday’s game against the Spurs, so Grimes will likely return to a bench role in their next game.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Luka Dončić led the Lakers with 28 points (8-of-24 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, one steal and three three-pointers in a 109-94 win over the Jazz on Monday.
body: Dončić didn’t have his best shooting night, but he did enough to lead the Lakers in scoring and to a second straight win. They were also able to get some revenge after Utah ended their nine-game win streak last week. Dončić is still putting up strong numbers, but he has cooled off a bit after his scorching hot start to the season. They’ll take on the Spurs on Friday in what will be a battle for first place in the West.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Ace Bailey posted a full line on Monday with 18 points (8-of-16 FGs), five rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Lakers.
body: Bailey continues to provide well-rounded value in his second season, and he has shown tremendous growth. He did a little bit of everything in this game, though it wasn’t enough for Utah to get the win. Bailey will continue to be a solid producer with Lauri Markkanen (wrist) still sidelined for a while longer. He hasn’t had many big games, but he has been consistent.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Kyle Filipowski provided a boost off the bench with 21 points (8-of-14 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), 12 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in a 109-94 loss to the Lakers on Monday.
body: Filipowski wasn’t in the rotation to start the season despite Jusuf Nurkić being sidelined, which was concerning. However, he was able to take advantage of his opportunity in this game. He set season highs for points, rebounds and assists while recording his first double-double of the season. It took Nurkić and Jaxson Hayes being out for him to get minutes, so this doesn’t make him a must-add, though he’s worth keeping an eye on to see how he fits into the rotation moving forward.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Mo Bamba started on Monday and contributed six points (3-of-7 FGs), seven rebounds, two assists and two blocks against the Lakers.
body: Bamba got the starting nod with Jaxson Hayes (knee) sidelined for this game. However, he wasn’t able to replicate his production from his last few games as a starter. He played 29 minutes, but he was thoroughly outplayed by Kyle Filipowski, who played less than 24 minutes off the bench. It seems Bamba’s strong stretch as a starter wasn’t actually going to lead to him being a fantasy stud for the rest of the season. Who knew?
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Zach LaVine recorded 18 points (8-of-17 FGs), six rebounds, two assists, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Spurs.
body: On a night when backcourt partner Darius Acuff Jr. (12 points, one rebound and four assists) went 5-of-14 from the field, LaVine shot a solid percentage and scored 18 points. Since going off for 31 points in a November 10 loss to the Magic, the veteran guard has scored 19 points or less in five straight games. However, LaVine’s fantasy value remains strong, as he’s exceeded his ADP (103) by a few rounds in nine-cat formats.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Andre Hunter amassed 15 points (7-of-12 FGs), seven rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Spurs.
body: After dishing out eight assists total in his prior three appearances, Hunter matched that number on Monday. Those eight assists were double his previous high this season, and Hunter was also valuable to fantasy managers as a scorer and rebounder. However, as has been the case for most of his NBA career, Hunter’s inability to provide defensive stats keeps his fantasy value low.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keegan Murray accounted for 14 points (6-of-12 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Spurs.
body: After grabbing at least seven rebounds in three straight games, Murray recorded just two on Monday. Given Sacramento’s offense, he has to do more in areas outside of scoring to provide reliable fantasy value. That hasn’t happened consistently enough, which is why Murray’s fantasy value sits well outside the top-100 in nine-cat formats.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Domantas Sabonis finished Monday’s loss to the Spurs with 20 points (8-of-9 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), 12 rebounds and eight assists.
body: Despite foul trouble, Sabonis had one of his most productive nights of the season on Monday. The Kings center finished two assists shy of a triple-double and recorded his fourth 20-point game of the season. While establishing chemistry with rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. has been a struggle at times, Sabonis remains a valuable center in fantasy basketball, regardless of league format. The Kings play two more games in Week 6, starting with the Warriors on Wednesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brandon Miller (knee) is available to play against the Grizzlies on Monday.
body: As expected, Miller has officially been cleared to play after initially being listed as probable. He briefly exited from Friday’s game against the Hawks, but he was able to return to finish that game and will continue to suit up against Memphis.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Duncan Robinson (quad) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Magic.
body: Robinson should be re-evaluated sometime this week, but he will not play on Tuesday. Kevin Huerter has moved into the starting lineup and should remain there until Robinson is available.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Duren (hamstring) has been ruled out against the Magic on Tuesday.
body: Duren was set to be re-evaluated on Sunday, and while there hasn’t been another update to his status, he won’t return against Orlando. Hopefully they provide a new timeline for him soon, but it looks like John Collins will get another start at center, with Paul Reed filling out the backup minutes down low.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Cade Cunningham (knee) is probable for Tuesday’s game against the Magic.
body: Cunningham’s right knee has been an issue for a little while now, but he’s only missed one game. The probable tag suggests that he’ll be available on Tuesday. If not, Daniss Jenkins’ role would likely expand.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Paul George (rest) is not on the injury report for Tuesday’s game against the Wizards.
body: George will be back after getting a rest night on the second leg of Boston’s back-to-back on Sunday. Jayson Tatum got the night off on Saturday, which allowed Sam Hauser to start both games. Hauser will head back to the bench against Washington.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Mitchell Robinson (illness) has been ruled out against the Wizards on Tuesday.
body: This will be a third straight absence for Robinson. Neemias Queta should continue to take on a few extra minutes at center, with Luka Garza filling out the backup minutes down low.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jaxson Hayes (knee) has been ruled out against the Lakers on Monday.
body: Hayes exited early on Sunday and will be held out for the second leg of Utah’s back-to-back. Mo Bamba, who had been on fire with Hayes out previously, should return to the starting lineup.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Ryan Dunn (quad) is available for Monday’s matchup with the Pelicans.
body: Dunn made an early exit Friday against the Jazz, but he’s in good shape following a weekend of rest. Dunn should continue to see his usual allotment of minutes off the bench.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Bryce McGowens (elbow) is available for Monday’s matchup with the Suns.
body: McGowens is back in action following a five-game absence, but his availability isn’t particularly meaningful to fantasy hoops managers given his limited role in New Orleans’ rotation.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Alex Caruso (hip) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Pacers.
body: Caruso joins a number of Thunder players on an extensive injury report, including Nikola Topic (hip) which means OKC will have to get creative with its lineups. Guys like Bennett Stirtz, Nique Clifford and Josh Dix could all see additional minutes.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Brandin Podziemski recorded a team-high 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds and two assists over 37 minutes to lead the Warriors to an 88-87 win over the Celtics on Sunday.
body: Podziemski helped Golden State snap a five-game losing streak in a low-scoring slugfest where both teams shot below 40 percent from the floor and failed to reach 90 points. He knocked down a clutch three-pointer to put the Warriors ahead with just over two minutes left on the clock and they managed to hold off the Celtics the rest of the way. He’ll continue to play an increased role while Stephen Curry remains sidelined with a partially-torn oblique. The Warriors have a three-game week on tap that includes matchups against the Kings, Trail Blazers and Clippers.
author: George Bissell

headline: Jayson Tatum amassed 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, six assists and one steal over 38 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: Tatum scored 23 first-half points to pass Bill Russell for eighth place on the franchise’s all-time scoring list and keep Boston within striking distance. It wasn’t enough as he went ice-cold in the second half as the Celtics dropped their fourth straight game. He missed a critical free throw in the final minute before failing to nail a wide-open three-pointer that would’ve put the Celtics ahead in the final 30 seconds. He had a chance to deliver a game-winner following a huge steal by Hugo González, but missed a fadeaway over Draymond Green. The 28-year-old fantasy star has delivered second-round value this season, averaging 26.4 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.7 assists, 0.7 steals and 0.7 blocks through 15 games. The Celtics have a three-game week coming up featuring showdowns against the Wizards, Hawks and Spurs.
author: George Bissell

headline: Charles Bassey chipped in 13 points (6-of-7 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists and three steals over 26 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Celtics.
body: Bassey delivered double-digit points for the third consecutive start shortly after Warriors head coach Steve Kerr told reporters that he wants to give Bassey an extended opportunity at center with Draymond Green moving to power forward. The decision paid dividends as Bassey came within one board of his second straight double-double. The well-traveled 26-year-old big man has looked like a viable fantasy option recently and is a worthwhile pickup in deeper formats. The Warriors have a three-game week coming up that includes matchups against the Kings, Trail Blazers and Clippers.
author: George Bissell

headline: Derrick White notched 14 points (6-of-21 FGs), three rebounds, five assists and one steal over 31 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: White was held scoreless in the opening half, but knocked down a couple clutch buckets in the final five minutes of regulation. He was open a couple times in the final minute but passed on those looks to feed Jayson Tatum, who missed a pair of potential go-ahead shots. He finished just 2-of-12 from three-point range and is shooting below 30 percent for the season from that range. The Celtics struggled to find secondary scoring to complement Tatum with Paul George sitting out for load management reasons on the second night of a back-to-back. The Celtics have a three-game week coming up featuring showdowns against the Wizards, Hawks and Spurs.
author: George Bissell

headline: Ivica Zubac tallied 10 points (5-of-11 FGs), 14 rebounds and one assist in Sunday’s loss to the Knicks.
body: Zubac recorded his sixth double-double of the season on Sunday, but unfortunately, there were no defensive stats to speak of. Entering the season with a fifth-round ADP, the 7-footer’s production has underwhelmed, and he ranks outside the top-100 in nine-cat formats. Of course, Tyrese Haliburton’s hamstring injury hasn’t helped, and many of Zubac’s other Pacers teammates have been affected as well, to no one’s surprise. Getting Haliburton back, which could happen by the end of November, would be huge for all the Pacers, including Zubac.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Andrew Nembhard recorded 16 points (5-of-13 FGs, 4-of-7 FTs), two rebounds, eight assists and two three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Knicks.
body: Nembhard led the way for the Pacers with eight assists, but he also committed six turnovers. While Braden Smith (6/1/4) gave the Pacers solid minutes off the bench, the absence of Tyrese Haliburton or T.J. McConnell to play off of tends to hurt Nembhard’s efficiency. Sitting just outside the top-100 in nine-cat formats, Nembhard’s current production aligns with his preseason ADP (117).
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kelly Oubre Jr. amassed 15 points (4-of-10 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs) and five rebounds in Sunday’s loss to the Knicks.
body: Oubre’s ability to get to the foul line gave his point total a welcome boost, but his overall production was underwhelming. Over the last two weeks, the Pacers’ wing has been a top-100 player, but the season-long value remains relatively low. The Pacers play three games in Week 6, starting with the Thunder on Monday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Pascal Siakam finished Sunday’s loss to the Knicks with 25 points (9-of-22 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals and three three-pointers.
body: While he didn’t shoot a high percentage, Siakam extended his streak of games with at least 20 points to four on Sunday. In fact, he last scored fewer than 19 points on November 1. While Tyrese Haliburton’s hamstring injury has changed the equation for the entire Pacers’ rotation, Siakam’s fantasy value has held steady. Given what happened last season, most fantasy managers will take that.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Josh Hart finished Sunday’s win over the Pacers with 10 points (5-of-11 FGs), 11 rebounds, 10 assists and one steal.
body: Having struggled for much of the season’s first month, Hart needed a night like Sunday. It was a historic one: he recorded his 18th triple-double for the Knicks. That moved him into a tie for second place on the franchise’s all-time list with the late Michael Ray Richardson, and Hart trails Walt Frazier by five for the top spot. Even if the shots aren’t falling, Hart can provide solid fantasy value, which is why he’s still rostered in 79 percent of Yahoo leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Landry Shamet amassed 17 points (7-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.
body: Back in the Knicks’ starting lineup for a second straight night, Shamet had another productive outing. He’s made at least two three-pointers in five straight games, and the veteran guard has provided reliable late-round fantasy value over the last two weeks. Rostered in 15 percent of Yahoo leagues, Shamet is worth streaming as long as OG Anunoby (calf) is out.
author: Raphielle Johnson
